findings: SNL56 lists one SH664A elbow, one SH664B nut and one SH664C sleeve for each of four bearing caps.
Original SNL86 identifies SH664A as Herring Motor Co. type69F; original SNL126 identifies SH664B as type61F. Both standalone rows have quantity4 and name M294/M298 as receivers.
SNL56 calls SH664C a Herring Motor Co. type60F sleeve. No dimension for its actual outside diameter, bore, length or seating taper is given in these inspected rows.

Original SNL67:035 lists a separate brass quarter-inch pipe collet, ordnance A16323, vehicle quantity12, with uses including M298 and SH664A. Survey identity P_a1f277f36b544171 is distinct from SH664C P_003a30f151b31d29. Possible overlap of sleeve/collet terminology needs reviewed evidence; do not silently merge or superimpose both at the same receiver.

The quarter-inch pipe/fitting nominal label alone does not establish a6.35mm outside diameter or a modern NPT thread. Treat fitting envelope, seat and passages as explicit unknowns until a source/cross-section constrains them.

HB20Plate11 shows an external pipe/fitting approaching the lower side of the cap and a separate opening near the top of the casting, while the cup holds wool. The exact internal oil route and inlet assignments need reconstruction against section evidence.

Original SNL261/262 explicitly specifies quarter-inch OUTSIDE diameter for B101960U/T/X/W copper tubes feeding the four bearing caps. This supports a6.35mm tube receiving envelope without treating the generic fitting nominal label as an OD or thread standard.

Each oil tube assembly includes a separate A16309 lubricator-end elbow, A16323 collet and SH102E union, in addition to the SH664A/B/C cap fitting set. This provides another location for the collet; exact end ownership and any SH664C interchangeability remain unqualified. Do not add a duplicate collet within the cap sleeve seat.
Original SNL274 gives eight ounces total wool and SNL56 two ounces per cap. Represent four porous material envelopes, each annotated2oz, not eight discrete solid parts or an inferred density.

Original HB18/19 confirms the cap cups contain wool for gradual feed to the four main bearings. A mechanical lubricator supplies those bearings and roller pinion shaft. Original sectionPlate22 supports the forward cup adjoining the bearing but does not dimension the oil drilling.

Candidate uses a front cup-wall inlet with upward-facing elbow connection, and a low horizontal gallery from the cup through cap and front lining to the sleeve running surface. Exact inlet side, gallery route/diameter and fitting shapes remain explicit reconstruction assumptions.

Only local cap fittings, porous wool volumes and bearing-feed galleries are populated in this increment. Full source-length armored oil lines and lubricator remain for subsequent connected-system work; no short tube stubs stand in for those complete source parts.
